name: Extended Teaching Dimension
definition: The **extended teaching dimension** is $$\mathrm{XTD}(\mathcal{H}) := \max_{f\subseteq\mathcal{X}}\min\left\{|S|:S\subseteq\mathcal{X},\;\left|\{h\in\mathcal{H}:h\cap S=f\cap S\}\right|\leq 1\right\}.$$ Thus the target labeling $f$ need not belong to $\mathcal{H}$.
description: Equivalently, it is the largest minimum size of a specifying set for an arbitrary labeling with respect to the class. For finite binary classes it equals the star number.
graph_summary: Maximum specifying-set size for an arbitrary target labeling; for finite binary classes, equal to the star number.

monotonic.proof: If $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, every specifying set for a target labeling with respect to $\mathcal H$ is also specifying with respect to $\mathcal G$, since the set of consistent hypotheses can only shrink. Minimize for each target and then maximize over targets.

p_monotonic.proof: For finite binary classes, XTD equals Star Number by Theorem 13 of \cite{hanneke2015minimax}; the latter is projection monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: For any target labeling on a conditioned fibre, extend it with the fixed labels.  A specifying set in the original class may discard fixed coordinates and still specifies the target in the fibre; hence XTD is c-monotonic.

doubly_monotonic.proof: It is monotonic under both subfamilies and coordinate projections.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: For finite binary classes, XTD equals Star Number. The six-concept Star-Number counterexample $\{001,010,011,100,101,110\}$ has value 2 on the full class and both one-coordinate conditioned fibres, so strict c-monotonicity fails.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: Tight strict c-monotonicity implies strict c-monotonicity, which fails for XTD.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity implies strict c-monotonicity, which fails for XTD.
